verses.1: And the king became angry. He stood on the doorstep and said, “My son Absalom, my son Absalom! Who will give me death? I will be under your control, Absalom, my son.”
verses.2: And Joshua saw that the king was crying and mourning over Abishalom.
verses.3: And on that day, there was a great sorrow for all the people. For on that day, the people heard that the king was sad over his sons.
verses.4: And on that day, the people would attack the city, just as the enemy soldiers attacked them in battle.
verses.5: And the king turned his face away. The king cried out in a loud voice, “Son of Abshalom! Son of Abshalom!”
verses.6: And Yoab went before the king and said, “Today, you must destroy the faces of all your servants who are carrying your soul. Today, you must also destroy the souls of your sons and daughters, as well as the souls of your wives and concubines.”
verses.7: To love those who hate you, and to be loved by those who hate you. For today you have shown that you have no servants or slaves. Today I know that Abshalom is alive, but we all die. Then it will be right in your eyes.
verses.8: And now, get up and speak to your servants from the heart. For in Jehovah I am praised, because you do not leave this place. If anyone tries to harm you tonight, it will be a great evil for you, after all the evil that has been done to you by your enemies since ancient times.
verses.9: And the king stood in the doorway. He said to all the people, “Look! The king is standing in the doorway.” Then all the people came forward before the king. And Israel saw a miracle done by the king.
verses.10: And all the people said, “The king has saved us from our enemies. He has delivered us from the hands of the Philistines. Now, let him go away from this land, from Abshalom.”
verses.11: And Absalom, who was killed in battle. Now, why do you still try to bring back the king?
verses.12: And King David sent messengers to Zedek and Ebiatar, the priests, saying, “Speak to the elders of Judah and tell them that they should return the king to his house.” And all the people came before the king’s house.
verses.13: Brothers, you are yourselves. By my words, you are brothers. Why then should you be enemies in order to restore the king?
verses.14: And to the Levites, you shall say: “May God do this for me. If you do not serve as leaders among the people, then I will be under their control every day.”
verses.15: And he filled the hearts of all the Jews with one thought. Then they sent him back to the king, along with all his servants.
verses.16: And the king sat down and went to Jerusalem and Judea. Then the messenger came to see the king, in order to bring the king back from Jerusalem.
verses.17: And Shimei, son of Gera, my right-hand man, who was among the chosen ones, went down with a Jew named Yehuda to see King David.
verses.18: And a thousand men were with him from Benyamin and Zivah. There was also a young man from the house of Shaul, along with twelve of his sons, and forty of his servants. They crossed the Jordan before the king.
verses.19: And he went through the doorway of the king’s house, and did what was right in his eyes. And Shemaiah son of Gerah fell before the king as he passed by the river.
verses.20: And he said to the king, “Do not consider me a threat. Do not remember what happened when your servant was called upon on that day when the king of Israel left Jerusalem to go to Lembas.”
verses.21: For your servant knows that I have sinned. And now, today, I come before the throne of the Lord, to receive judgment from Him.
verses.22: And Abishai son of Saruya said, “Under this, Shimei will not die, for he has rejected the Lord’s Messiah.”
verses.23: And David said, “What is this I hear? That you, sons of Zeruya, will become my enemies. Today, a man will die in Israel because I didn’t know that today I would be king over Israel.”
verses.24: And the king said to Shimei, “Do not die.” Then the king comforted him.
verses.25: And Phinoth son of Shaul went down to see the king. He did not wash his feet or clothes, and he did not change his clothes from that day until the day he returned.
verses.26: And it happened that when he came to Jerusalem to see the king, the king asked him, “Why didn’t you go with me?”
verses.27: And the king said to his servant, “I am proud of my servant. He has done a great service for me. I will ride on that chariot and go away from here.”
verses.28: And he shall go before your servant to the king. The king, who is like God himself, will do what is right in your eyes.
verses.29: For not every house of my father’s family was safe; only those who were slaves to the king remained alive. They ate your offerings and your gifts. What more can I do? I still have to cry out to the king for help.
verses.30: And the king said to him, “Why do you still speak those words? I have already said that you and Ziba will divide up the land.”
verses.31: And Mefiboset said to the king, “I will also take everything after Adonai, the king, comes back safely to his house.”
verses.32: And from the iron pillars, Gilad descended from above. He passed by King Yarden and sent him away.
verses.33: And in the bronze statue, there was an old man, son of Semonim. He was very old. He ruled over the king while he was in his tent. He was indeed a great man.
verses.34: And the king said to Barzillai, “You go ahead of me, and I will accompany you to Jerusalem.”
verses.35: And Barzillai said to the king, “How many days remain in my life? I will surely take the king to Jerusalem.”
verses.36: At the age of thirty, I will know whether it is good or bad for your servant to eat what he eats and to drink what he drinks. Will my servant still be able to hear the voices of singing and dancing? And why should my servant still go to the king’s court?
verses.37: Even though your servant will cross the Jordan and meet with the king, why will the king reward me for this great service?
verses.38: Please let your servant live in my city, along with the remains of my father and mother. And see, your servant will go through this place along with the king’s officials. Do whatever you think is right for him.
verses.39: And the king said, “Let him go ahead of them. I will do what is right in your eyes, and everything you command me to do, I will carry out.”
verses.40: And all the people crossed the Jordan. The king also crossed over, and he blessed Barzillai. Then he returned to his place.
verses.41: And the king passed through Gilgal, and all the people of Judah also went with him. Half of Israel also followed along with them.
verses.42: And behold, all the people of Israel came to the king and said to him, “Why have your brothers, the Jews, been taken away? They have crossed over the Jordan River, along with all the men of David’s household.”
verses.43: And every Jew in Judah said to the people of Israel, “The king has sent for us. Why do you refuse to do this? We have eaten from the king’s food. If you take us away with you, we will go with you.”
verses.44: And the man of Israel rebelled against the man of Judah. He said, “Give me ten days as king over you. I am also from your people. But know this: My words will not be listened to. I will not be able to restore my kingdom.” Then the man of Judah refused to listen to the man of Israel’s words.
